description:
A protocol callback's InputDemand is the join over the implementations DEFINED SO FAR
(collect_protocol_callback_node reads ProtocolDispatch Current). An implementation module
is defined only when some receiver needs it (resolve_protocol_call, jobs/semantic.rs
~1311-1333), so the callback's answer rises as implementations land
(ProtocolDispatch #1 -> #2), and every forwarder's answer and every activation keyed on
it moves after publication.

Measured on 00420: 5 InputDemand answers move after publication on fz-afu.3; 13 with
fz-afu.10's composition (Enumerable.count/1, reduce/3, reduce_while/3 and their
forwarders), costing AnalyzeActivation 888 -> 898 (authorized raise, 2026-09-26).

Refuted cure (probed): a callback waits for ModuleDefined of every provider in
ProtocolImplProviders. It removes every empty/flip-only AnalyzeActivation run
(00420 888 -> 877) but defines unused implementations: take 775 -> 998 jobs,
00181 296 -> 504, predicate_search 1796 -> 1913.

The honest answer is "the implementations this caller's receivers can reach", which
static demand cannot know without semantic analysis, which needs the demand. Needs a
paper-first design before any build. Close by restoring the 00420 work_start pin to at
most 2794.
title: A protocol callback's demand rises as implementations land
